color.description: the color the room was shown in in the zx spectrum original game. This is used to provide highlight colours in each room

height.description: custom room height that can be set per-room in blocks. If not set, the default room height is used. Only a few of the original game rooms need this to make the transition to the next room above work better. Can be used to fine-tune the point in a jump where the room above loads.

was.description: it is the bubbles that play the sound when something is fading out, not the item itself. This property helps us know which sound to play

disabled.description: disabled buttons can't be pressed until a controller enables them

type.description: this button targets items in the room. This is the default, so also used if undefined

disabled.description: disabled buttons can't be pressed until a controller enables them

speed.description: speed multiplier — undefined is treated as 1 (original game speed)
speed multiplier — undefined is treated as 1 (original game speed)

toDoor.description: the id of the door in the destination room. This usually does not need to be given since the game can choose the door facing the right way from the destination room. only give this if there are multiple doors in the same direction between the two rooms

delay.description: how long to delay until the first emitting? after this time the first emit will happen, then all others will continue at the period interval. undefined is treated the same as 0

emits.description: what does this emitter emit? Could be (potentially) any free item

maximumAtOnce.description: How many items emitted from this emitter can be in the room at once? If undefined, no limit. If already this many items in the room, the items will have to be removed from the room before more can be emitted (for example, collecting an emitted pickup)

offset.description: offset in blocks applied to the emission position, relative to the emitter's origin

sound.description: The sound to play on emit, undefined to use the default sound, or null for no sound

times.description: size of the emitter's collision volume in blocks; if undefined, the emitter has no volume

whenPlayerInside.description: if true, only emits while the currently selected player overlaps the emitter's bounds; timing resets on each entry

floorType.description: the room has no floor, but it is included to draw the floor edge

activated.description: if the lamp starts activated (shining) when the room loads. undefined is treated as true

direction.description: the direction the lamp shines its light beam in, when activated

times.description: lamps can be stacked to double/triple height - a beam is then emitted from every block of the stack

orientation.description: the initial orientation of the mirror's plane

times.description: mirrors can be stacked to double/triple height - the whole stack is one pane that flips together

disabled.description: disabled switches can't be toggled until a controller enables them

type.description: this switch targets items in the room. This is the default, so also used if undefined

disabled.description: disabled switches can't be toggled until a controller enables them

type.description: this switch targets the redux store

disabled.description: If true, the timer will start deactivated until a controller enables it. Default is false (activated on load)

tiles.description: the tiles to show - the length of this array also determines the size of the wall

items.description: by keying each item with an id, it makes the diffing easier since the array is no longer position-dependent

roomDecoration.description: a decorative set piece to draw into this room on the map

gridPosition.description: the grid position (on the map) of this sub-room

physicalPosition.description: where the sub-room actually starts and ends once loaded (so we can work out which sub-room items are in while the game is in-play)

subRooms.description: subRooms are used for the map for rooms which were modelled as multiple rooms in the original game, or for the whole room in some cases to preserve same-shame between big and small rooms

delay.description: how long to delay until the first emitting? after this time the first emit will happen, then all others will continue at the period interval. undefined is treated the same as 0

maximumAtOnce.description: How many items emitted from this emitter can be in the room at once? If undefined, no limit. If already this many items in the room, the items will have to be removed from the room before more can be emitted (for example, collecting an emitted pickup)

r5.description: what does this emitter emit? Could be (potentially) any free item

r11.description: if given, the item disappears after the specified interaction. This must be null (not undefined) so switches can tell the difference between having no setting, and having a setting to change to null when they make something not disappearing

toRoom.description: note that if the other room contains exactly one teleporter, we need not give the position or the item If undefined, is a same-room teleporter

toItemId.description:
an item in the destination room this teleporter should go to - the player will be moved to atop this item

If not given, will find the (only teleporter) in the destination room

note: not RoomItemId because that is the ids of items in *this* room, but this is pointing to another room

toRoom.description: note that if the other room contains exactly one teleporter, we need not give the position or the item.

r19.description: if given, the item will disappear only if stood/touched by items of this type. Eg, set to ['head', 'heels', 'headOverHeels'] to make only when touched by the player or ['head'] eg for doughnuts that only head can collect

appearanceRoomTime.description: the room time when this floating text starts; used to calculate the rise animation age. if not given, will start right away at time zero. if given, will delay starting until this time

makesStable.description: if true, equivalent to leftState disappearing on stand, right state not disappearing if false, equivalent to leftState not disappearing, right state disappearing on stand

r36.description: true is a shorthand for monsters/platforms that are activated by default:   {leftState: {activated: true, everActivated:true}, rightState: {activated:false}}, false is shorthand for monsters/platforms that are deactivated by default:   {leftState: {activated: false}, rightState: {activated: true, everActivated:true}},

r37.description:
The item will be removed from the room after the room it is in has more than this roomTime. To guarantee removal on the next frame (effectively immediately) set to -1. Otherwise, can set to the current roomTime + duration of an animation that needs to play

If null, the item is not scheduled for removal (the normal case)

r38.description:
where in the destination room this teleporter should go - usually to atop another teleporter, but could be anywhere.

If not given, will find the (only teleporter) in the destination room

r42.description: true is a shorthand for charles bots that are activated by default:   {leftState: {activated: true}, rightState: {activated: false}}, false is shorthand for charles bots that are deactivated by default:   {leftState: {activated: false}, rightState: {activated: true}},

flip.description: this switch will flip the other switch when it is flipped

r45.description: true is a shorthand for lamps that start activated (shining):   {leftState: {activated: true}, rightState: {activated: false}}, false is shorthand for lamps that start deactivated:   {leftState: {activated: false}, rightState: {activated: true}},

r46.description: true is a shorthand for conveyors that the switch enables   {leftState: {disabled: false}, rightState: {disabled: true}}, false is a shorthand for conveyors that the switch disables   {leftState: {disabled: true}, rightState: {disabled: false}},

r47.description: true is a shorthand for deadly blocks that start disabled:   {leftState: {disabled: true}, rightState: {disabled: false}}, false is a shorthand for deadly blocks that start enabled:   {leftState: {disabled: false}, rightState: {disabled: true}},

r48.description: true is a shorthand for disabling in the left setting:   {leftState: {disabled: true}, rightState: {disabled: false}}, false is a shorthand for disabling in the right setting:   {leftState: {disabled: false}, rightState: {disabled: true}},

r59.description: true means the left setting reverses the conveyor (opposite of config direction), false means the right setting reverses it. "reverse" = set direction to the opposite of the item's config.direction.

r63.description: item ids of all the items (probably Charles) that this joystick controls. if omitted, the joystick controls every charles in its room — which is how the original game always behaved.

r66.description: activated for us is a boolean, not the many-states from the json config, ie it is stateful on if the item is currently activated (so they can render differently)

r69.description: if this item has ever been activated, in the lifetime of the room. Charging cybermen will have this flag as false so long as they are charging

r76.description: the way the mirror turns (90°, to its other orientation) every time its controller changes setting

r78.description: shortcut - gives this direction for left state and opposite direction for right state

r85.description: the lines of text to display, each rendered as a separate row

r90.description: if true, the lamp is shining (emitting its light beam)

r92.description: if true, lines oscillate horizontally as they rise

r93.description: how many total should this emitter emit? Null for no limit
